short_answer: Winning Points is a real, long running football newsletter run by a named New York company with a street address and toll free number. Its issues were still being shared and tracked on betting forums in 2023 and 2024. In that sense it is a legitimate publication, not a phantom tout.

What it sells today is unclear. On 16 Nov 2026 the online signup page listed no products, the home page asked readers to call for information on 2025 football, its security certificate had expired and its home page showed database errors. A forum tracker that grades newsletter picks showed no Winning Points plays graded for the 2026 season as of 10 Nov 2026.

On results, the outside numbers we found point to roughly break even picking before the vig, which means a loss at normal odds. A rival newsletter's six season table put Winning Points best bets at 49.13%, and a forum tally of the 2022 season came to 29 wins and 33 losses. Readers mostly describe it as useful reading material, not a betting service to follow blindly.
pricing_intro: We found no price on 16 Nov 2026. The membership signup page showed no products, and the FAQ describes plan types (monthly, six months, full year and single issue access) without prices. The site also lists a 1-900 pick line and a toll free number for phone plays, with no rates shown.
pricing: Online membership (monthly, 6 months, full year, single issue)

Monthly plans renew automatically; cancel at least 2 business days before renewal, per the FAQ

guarantee: We found no guarantee, refund promise or free extension anywhere on the pages we opened. The FAQ only explains how to cancel an automatic monthly renewal: at least two business days before the renewal date, from the member profile page.

Six month, full year and single issue plans do not renew automatically, according to the FAQ. Losses on bets are never covered by any newsletter, and they are usually far larger than the subscription price.

claims_note: The About page says the service started in 1970 but also that the newsletter has been on newsstands "for the past 32 years." The page appears not to have been updated in a long time, so neither number tells you much about the picks.
The 60% revenge claim has no dates, sample size or log behind it on the page. The sample issue offered to new readers dates from 2015 and leads with an 11 game run chosen by the publisher.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: no full, time stamped log of every Winning Points pick from the publisher. The closest thing is outside tracking.

A spring 2021 issue of Powers' Picks, a rival newsletter, printed a table of football newsletter results for the 2015 to 2020 regular seasons. It listed Winning Points Best Bets and Preferred plays at 236 and 234 with 10 pushes in college (50.21%), 190 and 207 with 10 pushes in the NFL (47.86%), and 426 and 441 with 20 pushes combined (49.13%). The rival ranked itself first in the same table, so it has an interest, but the method was the same for every newsletter listed.

On TheRX in Sep 2023 a member who tracks newsletters posted Winning Points results for the 2022 season: college 4 star 10 and 4, college 3 star 8 and 6, NFL 4 star 5 and 13, NFL 3 star 6 and 10 with 2 pushes. That adds up to 29 and 33. In the same tracker on SBR, every Winning Points line read 0 and 0 as of 10 Nov 2026, so no 2026 plays had been graded there.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Winning Points pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Winning Points performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the outside tallies we found put Winning Points near 49% to 50% on its top plays. On the Watchdog board on 16 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found no buyer reviews of Winning Points on review sites. What exists is forum talk from readers who follow football newsletters, plus pick trackers. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found about eight relevant forum posts on SBR, Covers and TheRX from 2020 to 2026, plus one rival newsletter's results table. Nobody described a billing problem, a refund fight or pushy sales calls, which are the common complaints about phone touts. Instead the talk is about whether the picks win. Readers treat Winning Points as one of the old newsletters, worth reading for stats and angles, and several warn against betting its picks blindly. One member in 2023 praised its prior season and a good start, but the tallies we could open show about break even or worse over the longer run. Its issues were widely shared free on forums in 2023 and 2024, so most posters may not be paying customers.
On TheRX, a member answering a claim that only two newsletters had winning records said Winning Points led the way the season before and had started the new season 3 and 1.

A tracker in the same thread posted the 2022 numbers: college plays were winning (10 and 4 on 4 star, 8 and 6 on 3 star) while NFL plays lost (5 and 13 on 4 star, 6 and 10 on 3 star). He listed the NFL 4 star among the worst records of that season.

On Covers, a bettor said he uses Pointwise, Winning Points and Northcoast. Another member replied that these are all losing publications, but that they can still be useful for stats and for reading the general consensus.
On SBR, when a member suggested several newsletters including Winning Points, another said they are only for reading and told people to think twice before betting the picks.

In the same SBR thread a longtime member said Pointwise and Winning Points have been around for decades but that "the print is too small for me." Another said the newsletters were posted free on the forum every week.

A weekly SBR tracker that grades the best bets of many newsletters showed every Winning Points category at 0 wins and 0 losses for the 2026 season, while it graded dozens of plays for other newsletters. It does not say why.
A Better Business Bureau search for Starpoint Publishing in New York returned no results. Our searches found no buyer review of a paid subscription on any forum we opened.

conflicts: The only multi season record we found was compiled and printed by Powers' Picks, a competing newsletter that ranked itself first. Its numbers for Winning Points may be accurate, but a rival is not a neutral auditor.

Full Winning Points issues were posted free on forums such as BookmakersReview by users in 2023 and 2024. That is not a conflict for the publisher, but it means many forum opinions come from readers, not paying subscribers.
strengths: A named company with a New York address, a toll free number, written legal terms and a clear FAQ on cancelling auto renewal.
Long history as a printed newsletter, with full weekly write ups on every board game rather than only a few picks.
No reports we found of billing disputes, refund fights or high pressure sales.
concerns: No products available for purchase on the site on 16 Nov 2026, and no prices shown anywhere.
Outside tallies put the top plays near 49% over six seasons, below the 52.4% needed at -110.
The site shows signs of neglect: an expired security certificate, database errors on the home page, a 2015 sample issue and a call line for 2025 football.
Seller claims such as a 60% revenge record come with no log or dates.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the date of the issue. A sample from 2015 is not a record.
Confirm what you are buying and what it costs before you give card details, since the site lists no prices.
If you take a monthly plan, note the renewal date and cancel at least two business days before it.
Count units, not wins. A 50% record at -110 loses money.
Use a newsletter as research, and record any pick you bet with the line you actually got.
faq: It is a real, long running newsletter published by a named New York company with an address and phone number. We found no court or regulator action and no billing complaints. Whether its picks win is another matter: the outside tallies we found put its best bets near 49% over six seasons.
How much does Winning Points cost?
We could not find a price. On 16 Nov 2026 the signup page said no products were available, and the phone lines list no rates.
Does Winning Points have a verified record?

Not from the publisher. A rival newsletter's table for the 2015 to 2020 regular seasons put its Best Bets and Preferred plays at 426 and 441 with 20 pushes, and a forum tracker counted 29 and 33 for 2022.

We could not confirm it. Issues were shared on forums in 2023 and 2024, but in 2026 the signup page sold nothing and a forum tracker had graded no Winning Points plays as of 10 Nov 2026. Call the listed number before paying.
